body:
Miguel Santos: Need to lock design partners for quantization profile library beta this week. Goal: 2–3 partners (hosted + dedicated mix). Also want to set expectations clearly: explicit enablement only, monitoring required, and rollback SLA/steps.

Marissa Cole: +1. criteria I’m thinking:
- already running steady prod traffic on Redwood (so we can measure cost/token)
- can isolate to a specific route (no “all traffic everywhere”)
- willing to run offline evals / accept a gated rollout
- okay with feature allowlist + feedback loop

Markus Klein: candidates from pipeline:
1) Acme AI (hosted) — already asked for route-level control + they have perf budget pressure
2) Northstar Search (dedicated) — cares about throughput + latency, has clear SLOs
3) Falconbank (private-ish / security heavy) — may be too much process for beta, but good for audit/RBAC validation

Paula Mendes: I’d prefer 1 hosted + 1 dedicated for the canary mechanics. Falconbank might be better for GA readiness (change control, approvals) unless we want them for “beta but behind extra guardrails”.

Connor O'Brien: from rollout/SRE perspective: keep beta simple. Partners must agree to:
- start with 0% (toggle set but not active), then 1% canary, then ramp
- watch dashboards for at least 30 min after each change
- allow us to disable route setting immediately if alerts trip
Kill-switch remains our backstop.

Dev Patel: Support needs an explicit “if anything looks off, here’s what you do” message we can send:
- how to tell if profile applied vs fallback
- where the change history is
- how to rollback (route disable first, then escalate for kill-switch)
If we don’t set that expectation, we’ll get “it changed output quality” tickets with no repro.

Aisha Bello: monitoring expectations I can share w/ partners (high level):
- fallback rate (should be ~0 for pinned pools)
- p95 latency delta vs baseline
- 5xx / timeout rate
- quality guardrail block events (we page internally; partners can see in dashboard)
We’ll also tag traces/logs with `quant_profile_id` so they can hand us request IDs.

Miguel Santos: ok but what do we promise on “rollback SLA”? we can’t commit to something legal-y in Slack, but we can set an operational expectation for beta.

Connor O'Brien: suggest wording:
- Partners can disable at route level themselves instantly (self-serve)
- Redwood oncall will respond and assist within 30 min during agreed beta hours
- In an active incident, we’ll pull kill-switch immediately (minutes)
But we should keep it as “best effort / operational target” unless it’s in the beta terms.

Naomi Feldman: +1 on not over-promising. For Falconbank specifically, they’ll ask about approvals + audit trails. We can say:
- route-level enablement requires appropriate RBAC (admin / route-config permission)
- changes are audited (actor, route, previous vs new setting)
- we can export audit logs on request
But for beta: no custom approval workflow.

Alex Martinez: for messaging, DevEx can provide a short beta “Getting Started + Risks” blurb:
- opt-in per route (no default-on)
- “recommended/latest” won’t auto-switch without user action (we should state this explicitly)
- how to run A/B eval playbook before ramping
I can draft a 1-pager for CSMs.

Markus Klein: re partner selection: Acme already offered to do weekly checkins + they can pin traffic to a single route. Northstar has dedicated pool pinned to GPU SKU, which reduces incompatibility edge cases.

Marissa Cole: agree. Falconbank is valuable but likely to slow us down in beta (security review, change control). We can keep them warm for GA design review.

Miguel Santos: proposal:
- Beta Partner #1: Acme AI (hosted)
- Beta Partner #2: Northstar Search (dedicated)
- Beta Partner #3 (stretch / limited scope): 1 more hosted customer with simpler setup OR keep slot open
Markus — do we have anyone else that’s “easy” besides those two?

Markus Klein: maybe “Juniper Notes” (mid-market SaaS) but they’re not in the quant thread. Acme + Northstar are the cleanest.

Paula Mendes: I’d rather do 2 partners well than 3 messy ones. If we do 3, require they accept the same rollout template and have someone to actually monitor.

Dev Patel: +1. fewer partners = less support load. but we should still document the expectation:
- they own enabling/disabling
- they notify us before ramping
- they keep baseline route available for quick compare

Aisha Bello: can we ask partners to keep a “baseline” route clone (same model/version) for A/B? That makes debugging way faster.

Marissa Cole: yes. Also ask them not to combine changes during beta (no prompt revamp + quant toggle same day). Otherwise we can’t attribute deltas.

Miguel Santos: drafting expectation email to partners. Key bullets:
1) Explicit opt-in per route; default behavior unchanged
2) Start at 1% canary; ramp only after Redwood confirms dashboards green
3) Monitoring: latency/5xx/fallback/quality guardrails; share request IDs if issues
4) Rollback: partner can disable immediately; Redwood will assist (target response within 30 min during beta hours); kill-switch if widespread
5) Weekly 30-min checkins + share benchmark results

Connor O'Brien: add “beta hours” explicitly. Example: Mon–Fri 9a–5p PT for changes. Outside that, no ramps.

Naomi Feldman: also add: “If you are in a regulated environment, beta is not a compliance feature.” (avoid confusion with Private/on-prem expectations).

Alex Martinez: I’ll send Miguel a draft snippet for the enablement + troubleshooting section today.

Miguel Santos: action items:
- Markus: confirm Acme + Northstar contacts + proposed kickoff times
- Paula: provide rollout template (0% → 1% → 10% → 50% → 100%) + success criteria
- Aisha/Connor: share the list of dashboard links + what “red” looks like (high level)
- Alex: 1-pager beta guidance for CSMs + partner-facing snippet
I’ll own the expectation email + calendar invites.

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: I’ll also add a “stop conditions” list (quality guardrail spike, p95 regression, load_error fallback) so partners know when we’ll ask to roll back.

Aisha Bello: I’ll DM Miguel a short monitoring checklist + screenshot of the dashboard filters (route/model/region). Keeping it simple for partners.

Markus Klein: ok, I’ll ping Acme + Northstar today and confirm they’re comfortable with: route clone for baseline, beta hours, and weekly checkins.

Connor O'Brien: thanks. pls make sure they understand: no silent changes. profile refs are pinned by version for beta. If we publish a new profile version, they won’t get it unless they opt in.

Miguel Santos: perfect, that line is going into the email verbatim.
